title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. Throughout this cote, c_{i,j} is almost certainly the binomial coefficient (i+j choose i), the structure constant of divided powers: x^{[i]} x^{[j]} = c_{i,j} x^{[i+j]}. The ξ_k (k ≥ 0) are elements of some Z_p-module, probably graded pieces of a class in a divided-power de Rham / crystalline-type computation. They satisfy relation (1) from the previous page: c_{l,i+j} ξ_{i+j} = c_{l,j} ξ_{i+j+l}, for a fixed i and all j, l ≥ 0. Any coefficient that is ≢ 0 (p) is a unit in Z_p, which is what lets one transfer vanishing from one ξ to another. 'Au voisinage de (1.1)' means: at the indices k = i+j with c_{i,j} ≢ 0 (p), i.e. no carry when adding i and j in base p (Lucas/Kummer).

Lemma 1 (finished on this page). Write i and j in base p up to digit r, with i_α + j_α ≤ p-1 for every α. Set j'_α = p-1-i_α. Then:
- i + j' = p^{r+1}-1;
- c_{i,j'} ≢ 0 and c_{j'-j,j} ≢ 0, since neither addition has a carry;
- therefore ξ_{i+j} = 0 ⇔ ξ_{p^{r+1}-1} = 0.
Do the same for a second admissible index k̄ = i + j̄, with the same r large enough, i.e. p^{r+1} > i, j, j̄. Comparing gives ξ_k = 0 ⇔ ξ_{k̄} = 0. So among the indices k ≥ N with c_{i,k-i} ≢ 0 (p), if one ξ_k vanishes, all do.

End of the proof (begins here). The goal is ξ_k = 0 for all k ≥ N. From (1), c_{ℓ,k} ξ_k = c_{ℓ,k-i} ξ_{k+ℓ}. So it suffices to find ℓ ≥ 0 with:
- c_{ℓ,k} ≢ 0 (p), so that ξ_k is a unit times something;
- c_{i,k+ℓ-i} ≢ 0 (p), so that k+ℓ is an admissible index and ξ_{k+ℓ} = 0 by Lemma 1.
With k = i+j, this is Lemma 2 on the next page: for any i, j there is ℓ with c_{i+j,ℓ} and c_{i,j+ℓ} both ≢ 0 (p). Take ℓ = p^m - 1 - (i+j) for m large. Then i+j+ℓ has all digits p-1, so the first addition has no carry. Also j+ℓ = p^m-1-i has digits p-1-i_α, so i + (j+ℓ) has no carry either. The marginal 'présentation plus simple' on the previous page is exactly this complement-to-p^m-1 trick.

The whole page is an elementary base-p carry argument, serving a vanishing statement in the divided-power de Rham computation.
errors: Notational slip: the text writes 'c_{k,k-i} ≢ 0 (p)' where the argument requires c_{i,k-i} ≢ 0 (p).
The line 'la condition que k, savoir c_{i,k'-i}=0' should read ≢ 0, the no-carry condition; this is most likely a transcription issue.
Minor indexing inconsistency between the margin of the previous page (p^r - 1 with p^r > i+j) and this page (p^{r+1} - 1). It is harmless, since r is arbitrary.
Implicit requirement: when comparing k and k̄, the same r must be used for both. This is satisfied by choosing r large, as Grothendieck indicates.

ideas.what: Transferring vanishing among the ξ_k via unit binomial coefficients, using base-p carry analysis.
ideas.modern_name: Lucas' theorem / Kummer's carry theorem applied to divided-power structure constants

ideas.what: Complementing an index to p^m - 1 (all digits p-1) so that two binomial coefficients are simultaneously prime to p (Lemma 2).

deep.surprise_reason: This is a correct but routine combinatorial lemma (Lucas/Kummer carries), an auxiliary step in a divided-power de Rham computation. Nothing on the page is conceptually new or absent from the literature.
transcription_corrections: 'tous le sont' should read 'tous le sont' / 'tous les ξ_k le sont'; '\tilde{k}' and '\bar{k}' denote the same second index.
